description: Nosso time é formado por um professor/tutor e alunos do segundo ano do Ensino Médio Técnico com Informatica do Colégio ETIP localizado na cidade de Santo André.
summary: We developed an interactive Mars mission simulator that challenges users to manage essential resources, maintain life-support systems, build facilities, and protect an astronaut throughout a 30-day mission. It addresses the challenges of space exploration by simulating real situations astronauts may face on Mars, such as limited resources, equipment failures, environmental hazards, and unexpected events. The project encourages problem-solving, strategic thinking, and resource management, helping users understand the complexity of sustaining human life beyond Earth.
details:
Our project is an interactive Mars mission simulator designed to demonstrate the challenges of sustaining human life on another planet. The player takes on the role of a mission manager responsible for keeping an astronaut alive during a 30-day mission on Mars. The game works by allowing players to manage essential resources such as water, oxygen, food, energy, and construction materials, while building facilities, repairing damaged equipment, and responding to random events like dust storms, water leaks, and system failures. Players have a limited number of actions each day, which makes planning and decision-making essential.

The main benefit of the project is that it provides an educational and interactive way to understand the difficulties of space exploration. It encourages critical thinking, problem-solving, resource management, and strategic planning. Its intended impact is to increase awareness of the challenges astronauts may face on Mars and show how important technology, preparation, and sustainability are for future space missions.

We developed the project using HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript, creating a browser-based experience. HTML structures the content, CSS handles the visual design and layout, and JavaScript controls the simulation, resource management, facilities, events, and game mechanics. We used Visual Studio Code as our code editor and a web browser to run and test the project. No specialized hardware was required.

The creative aspect of our project is the transformation of a complex topic like Mars exploration into an interactive survival experience. Instead of simply presenting information, we allow users to experience simulated mission challenges and understand the consequences of their decisions. During development, we considered resource limitations, astronaut health, habitat integrity, equipment efficiency, unexpected environmental events, game balance, and ease of use. These factors helped us create a simulation that is both educational and engaging, connecting programming concepts with real challenges related to human exploration of Mars.
